description: Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, is a beloved Indian classic featuring tender chicken pieces swimming in a rich, creamy tomato-based gravy. This iconic dish is known for its subtly sweet and tangy flavor profile, perfectly balanced with aromatic spices and a hint of smokiness. It is a comforting and luxurious meal, ideal for a special occasion or a delicious weeknight dinner.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine chicken pieces with plain yogurt, 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, 1 teaspoon red chili powder, turmeric powder, 1 teaspoon garam masala, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and lemon juice. Mix well to coat all pieces. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours for best flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Marinated Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of butter and 1 tablespoon of oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook for 5-7 minutes, turning occasionally, until the chicken is lightly browned and cooked through. Remove the cooked chicken from the pan and set it aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Gravy Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, add the remaining 3 tablespoons of butter. Add the finely chopped onion and sauté over medium heat until it turns translucent and soft, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the remaining 1 tablespoon of ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Add Tomatoes and Spices
instructions.text: Pour in the tomato puree or crushed tomatoes. Add the soaked cashews, remaining 1 teaspoon red chili powder, coriander powder, and cumin powder. Mix everything well. Cook this mixture for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the mixture thickens significantly and the oil begins to separate from the sides.

instructions.title: Blend the Gravy
instructions.text: Allow the cooked tomato-cashew mixture to cool slightly. Carefully transfer it to a blender. Add 1/2 cup of water and blend until the mixture is completely smooth. For an extra velvety texture, pass the blended gravy through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan, discarding any coarse residue.

instructions.title: Simmer and Season the Gravy
instructions.text: Return the pan with the smooth gravy to medium heat. Stir in the remaining 1/2 teaspoon garam masala, crushed Kasuri Methi, sugar or honey, and salt to taste. Bring the gravy to a gentle simmer, stirring frequently to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Combine Chicken and Finish
instructions.text: Add the previously cooked chicken pieces to the simmering gravy. Stir thoroughly to ensure the chicken is well coated with the rich sauce. Cook for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld beautifully. Finally, stir in the heavy cream and cook for just 1-2 minutes more, ensuring the gravy doesn't come to a rolling boil after adding the cream.

instructions.title: Garnish and Serve
instructions.text: Garnish the classic Butter Chicken generously with freshly chopped cilantro. Serve hot with warm naan bread, roti, or fragrant basmati rice for a complete and satisfying Indian meal.

tips: For an extra smooth and silky gravy, always blend the cooked tomato-onion-cashew mixture thoroughly and then pass it through a fine-mesh sieve. This removes any fibrous bits and ensures a restaurant-quality texture.

Do not skip the Kasuri Methi (dried fenugreek leaves). Crushing them between your palms before adding releases their unique, slightly bitter, aromatic flavor which is crucial for authentic Butter Chicken taste.

Butter Chicken tastes even better the next day as the flavors have more time to meld. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat gently on the stovetop or in the microwave.
article:
Butter Chicken Classic Murgh Makhani: Your Guide to a Creamy Indian Delight

Butter Chicken, known in India as Murgh Makhani, is arguably one of the most beloved and globally recognized Indian dishes. Its rich, creamy, and mildly spiced tomato-based gravy, combined with tender pieces of marinated chicken, creates a symphony of flavors that has captivated palates worldwide. Originating in Delhi, India, this classic dish has evolved into a staple in Indian restaurants and homes alike, offering a comforting and indulgent culinary experience. If you've ever wanted to recreate that restaurant-quality Butter Chicken experience in your own kitchen, this comprehensive guide will walk you through every step, ensuring a delicious and authentic result.

## What is Butter Chicken Classic Murgh Makhani?

At its heart, Butter Chicken Classic Murgh Makhani is a celebration of contrasting yet complementary flavors and textures. The name "Murgh Makhani" literally translates to "chicken with butter," hinting at the luxurious richness that defines the dish. It typically features succulent pieces of boneless chicken, often marinated in yogurt and spices, which are then either pan-fried, grilled, or cooked in a tandoor (a traditional clay oven) until slightly charred. This cooked chicken is then simmered in an incredibly smooth and luscious gravy made primarily from tomatoes, butter, and cream, along with aromatic Indian spices.

The magic of Butter Chicken lies in its balance. The tanginess of the tomatoes is mellowed by the sweetness of sugar, the richness of butter and cream, and the earthy warmth of spices like garam masala and fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi). While it’s typically mildly spiced, it's packed with flavor, making it a crowd-pleaser for those who prefer less heat but don't want to compromise on taste. Its vibrant orange-red hue is as inviting as its aroma, promising a truly satisfying meal.

## Ingredients You Need

To embark on your Murgh Makhani journey, gather these essential ingredients. Quality ingredients make a noticeable difference in the final taste of your Butter Chicken.

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken (thighs or breast), cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt (full-fat for best results)
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color, or regular for heat)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1 teaspoon salt
*   1 tablespoon lemon juice

For the Gravy:
*   2 tablespoons unsalted butter
*   1 tablespoon oil (vegetable or canola)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 (400g) can crushed tomatoes, or 3-4 medium fresh tomatoes, pureed
*   1/2 cup raw cashews (soaked in hot water for 15-20 minutes, then drained)
*   2 green chilies (optional, adjust to taste)
*   1 teaspoon coriander powder
*   1/2 teaspoon cumin powder
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder recommended)
*   1/4 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1 tablespoon kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed between palms
*   1 teaspoon sugar (or to taste, balances tomato acidity)
*   1 teaspoon salt (or to taste)
*   1/2 cup heavy cream
*   1/4 cup water (or as needed to adjust consistency)

For Garnish:
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped
*   A swirl of heavy cream

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Follow these steps carefully to create an exquisite Butter Chicken.

Step 1: Marinate the Chicken
In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients (yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, garam masala, salt, lemon juice). Mix well, ensuring each piece is coated. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 4-6 hours, or even overnight for maximum flavor penetration.

Step 2: Cook the Chicken
Heat a large pan or grill pan over medium-high heat. Add a tablespoon of oil. Once hot, add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook in batches if necessary. Sear the chicken for 3-4 minutes per side, until it's cooked through and has a slight char on the edges. This char adds a desirable smoky flavor. Remove the cooked chicken and set aside.

Step 3: Prepare the Gravy Base
In the same pan (or a separate heavy-bottomed pot), melt the butter with the remaining oil over medium heat. Add the finely chopped onions and sauté until they turn translucent and lightly golden, about 5-7 minutes. Add the ginger-garlic paste and green chilies (if using), and cook for another minute until fragrant.

Step 4: Build the Gravy Flavors
Stir in the crushed tomatoes (or fresh tomato puree) and the soaked, drained cashews. Add the dry spices: coriander powder, cumin powder, red chili powder, turmeric, and garam masala. Cook this mixture for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes have cooked down and the oil starts to separate from the mixture. This step is crucial for developing a deep flavor.

Step 5: Blend the Gravy
Remove the pan from the heat and let the mixture cool slightly. Carefully transfer the entire contents to a blender. Blend until absolutely smooth. For an ultra-silky, restaurant-style gravy, pass the blended mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean pot. This removes any remaining bits of onion, cashew, or tomato skin, resulting in a wonderfully smooth sauce.

Step 6: Finish the Gravy and Combine
Return the sieved gravy to the pot over medium-low heat. Add the kasoori methi (crushed between your palms to release its aroma), sugar, and salt. Stir well and simmer for 5 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.
Add the cooked chicken pieces to the simmering gravy. Stir gently to coat the chicken. Pour in the heavy cream and stir until combined. Do not boil vigorously after adding cream, as it can curdle. Simmer for another 2-3 minutes, just enough to heat the chicken through and allow it to absorb the gravy’s flavors.

Step 7: Garnish and Serve
Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary. Garnish your delicious Butter Chicken with a swirl of fresh cream and a sprinkle of chopped cilantro just before serving.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Achieving that perfect Butter Chicken isn't just about following steps; a few pro tips can elevate your dish from good to extraordinary.

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marination time. The longer the chicken marinates, the more tender and flavorful it will be. Overnight is ideal.
*   **Charred Chicken for Depth:** The slight char on the chicken pieces adds a crucial smoky depth that mimics tandoor-cooked chicken and is characteristic of authentic Murgh Makhani. Don't overcook it, though; keep it juicy.
*   **Smooth Gravy is a Must:** Blending the gravy base thoroughly is essential. For that velvety texture, straining the blended gravy through a fine-mesh sieve is highly recommended. It takes a little extra effort but makes a significant difference.
*   **Balance of Flavors:** Taste your gravy at different stages. Adjust the sugar to balance the acidity of the tomatoes and the salt to your preference. Kasoori methi is not optional; it imparts a unique, slightly bitter, aromatic note that is signature to Butter Chicken.
*   **Quality of Ingredients:** Use full-fat yogurt, good quality butter, and fresh heavy cream. These fats contribute significantly to the richness and mouthfeel of the dish.
*   **Don't Boil Cream:** Once you add the heavy cream, simmer the gravy gently. High heat can cause the cream to separate or curdle.

## Serving Suggestions

Butter Chicken is a versatile main course that pairs wonderfully with a variety of accompaniments.

*   **Naan Bread:** Hot, fluffy naan bread (garlic naan, butter naan, or plain naan) is the quintessential pairing. It's perfect for scooping up every last drop of the rich gravy.
*   **Basmati Rice:** Steamed basmati rice or fragrant jeera rice (cumin rice) provides a lovely contrast to the creamy curry, absorbing its flavors beautifully.
*   **Roti or Paratha:** For a lighter option, whole wheat roti or flaky paratha also work very well.
*   **Side Salad:** A simple side salad of sliced cucumbers, onions, and tomatoes, perhaps with a squeeze of lemon, offers a refreshing counterpoint to the richness of the Butter Chicken.
*   **Raita:** A cooling cucumber or mint raita (yogurt dip) can be a delightful accompaniment, especially if you've added a little extra spice to your Murgh Makhani.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Butter Chicken recipe is perfect as is, there are several ways to adapt it to dietary needs or personal preferences.

*   **Vegetarian/Vegan Options:**
    *   **Paneer Makhani:** Substitute chicken with paneer (Indian cottage cheese), cubed and lightly fried.
    *   **Tofu Makhani:** Use firm or extra-firm tofu, pressed, cubed, and pan-fried.
    *   **Vegan Butter Chicken:** Replace butter with plant-based butter, heavy cream with cashew cream (blended soaked cashews with water) or coconut milk, and yogurt with a plant-based alternative.
*   **Spice Level:** For more heat, increase the amount of red chili powder or add more green chilies. For a milder version, reduce them or omit the green chilies entirely. Kashmiri chili powder is excellent for color without excessive heat.
*   **Smoky Flavor Enhancement:** To impart a deeper smoky flavor, akin to a tandoor, you can use the "dhungar" method: heat a small piece of charcoal until red hot, place it in a small heatproof bowl within the gravy, pour a teaspoon of ghee over it, and immediately cover the pot for 5-10 minutes to infuse the smoke.
*   **Healthier Alternatives:** While Butter Chicken is an indulgent dish, you can make minor adjustments. Use Greek yogurt for marination, reduce the amount of butter and cream, or opt for low-fat cream. The flavor profile will shift slightly but still be delicious.
*   **Nut Substitutions:** If you have a cashew allergy, you can substitute cashews with blanched almonds for creaminess, or simply use more heavy cream or a touch of coconut milk (if you don't mind a slight coconut flavor).

Mastering Butter Chicken Classic Murgh Makhani is a rewarding culinary journey. With this detailed guide, you're well-equipped to create a truly authentic and unforgettable Indian dining experience right in your home kitchen. Enjoy the rich aromas and flavors of this beloved dish!
